newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa futures called to open $5 to $10 lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa futures called to open $5 to $10 lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $5 to $10 lower Wednesday as traders expect the market to follow through on Tuesday's weak finish.

New York cocoa futures tumbled Tuesday, pounded by chart-driven trade and speculative selling. Spot March futures slid $29 on the day to finish at $1,294 a tonne after ranging from $1,324 to $1,288. Most-active May shed $28 to $1,324, while the outer months finished $26 to $31 lower.

Technically, traders pegged March near-term support at $1,288-$1,282, with the next target seen around $1,259, its life-of-contract low. On the upside, they said March would face resistance at $1,316.

London cocoa futures were sharply lower early Wednesday on the heels of New York's steep losses. Benchmark LIFFE March cocoa fell 21 stg at the midday break, to 880 stg a tonne, while May was down 22 stg, to 902 stg. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodities Desk 212 859 1640))
